method: javap -c on the named 1.21.7 server jar for every vanilla method spot-checked (JigsawPlacement/Placer, StructurePoolElement, StructurePiece, PoolElementStructurePiece, SculkPatchFeature, SculkSpreader behaviours, MultiNoiseBiomeSourceParameterList Preset + OverworldBiomeBuilder, Aquifer fluid picker); exact data diffs of prepared resources vs jar (12 worldgen registries, 941 entries; structure NBTs 1202/1202; flat/world presets); paired chunk comparison port Test 1 vs vanilla Test World, same seed 8257987075890829262, 1,018 paired chunks (Nov 21 dumps — PRE-FIX code state, see report); decode-coverage audit of every worldgen dispatch arm; Batch 0 oracle-status triage for all 47 oracles referenced by the batch's 54 drivers (16 pass / 31 fail). No driver was run: 24 drivers have no oracle blocker (12 passing-oracle + 12 no-oracle) and are ready to run when the execution block lifts; 30 are blocked on failing oracles. Checks tally = 22 behaviour checks (18 pass, 4 gap) + 47 oracle status checks (16 pass, 31 fail).

items.evidence: Vanilla SculkPatchFeature.place (1.21.7 jar bytecode): after the spreader rounds, if random.nextFloat() <= catalystChance (0.5) and origin.below() is collision-full, sets SCULK_CATALYST at origin; then extraRareGrowths.sample(random) times places SCULK_SHRIEKER[can_summon=true] at origin.offset(nextInt(5)-2, 0, nextInt(5)-2) when air above a sturdy face. Port worldgen/sculk.rs place() ends after the spreader rounds; decode ignores catalyst_chance and extra_rare_growths; no 'catalyst' string anywhere in sculk.rs. Ancient-city templates contain zero catalysts (58 files: 10 sensors only), so all 1,278 vanilla catalysts come from sculk_patch. Explains the world-compare finding: sculk catalysts 0 (port) vs 1,278 (vanilla). The missing nextFloat/nextInt calls also shift the RNG stream for every feature placed after a sculk_patch in the same chunk — the likely mechanism behind the PORT-NOTES sculk-vein cell divergence (unconfirmed at HEAD). Affects sculk_patch_ancient_city (extra_rare_growths uniform 1..3) and sculk_patch_deep_dark (0). Spreader core itself verified faithful (all three behaviours match jar bytecode).
items.title: sculk_patch never places sculk catalysts or extra rare growths (catalyst_chance / extra_rare_growths ignored)

items.evidence: Vanilla base StructurePiece serializes genDepth as 'GD' (always 0 for jigsaw pieces: trial chambers 245/245 GD=0, village_plains 210/210 GD=0 in the reference world) alongside PoolElementStructurePiece's live 'ground_level_delta'. Port jigsaw.rs PoolPiece save writes ground_level_delta but no GD (grep: 'GD' appears only in end_city.rs and legacy.rs). Cosmetic: vanilla's loader reads only ground_level_delta (default 0) for pool pieces, so saves load fine; but a strict structure-start NBT comparison (test_structure_start_nbt_parity, currently oracle-blocked) would flag the missing key.
items.title: PoolPiece NBT omits the vestigial GD (genDepth) key vanilla writes

systemic_note: No single systemic cause across this batch's defects (unlike the pilot's tag pattern). B6-G01 is a dropped config tail (two fields silently ignored by decode — serde's unknown-field tolerance means a missing feature reads as success). B6-G02/G03 are measured-but-unroot-caused terrain divergences under separate investigation. The oracle failures share one pattern: the oracles were written against the 26.x API and 1.21.7 moved or never had those packages/signatures (densityfunction, material.rule, gizmos, gamerules, Feature ctor, BiomeManager.getBiome). Decode-coverage is complete (every dispatch arm present) but arm presence is not correctness — the one arm-level defect found (B6-G01) was a silent omission inside a present, well-tested arm, found only by javap-diffing the feature's tail.
out_of_scope_failures: None. Adjacent findings NOT recorded as B6 defects: (1) bubble columns 0 vs 2,500 — owned by the pilot as G1; (2) beds block entities 0 vs 50 in the world comparison — a save-format gap, not worldgen; (3) PORT-NOTES sculk-vein cell divergence and tuff-blob position divergence — unconfirmed at HEAD (old-world measurements; ore feature and sculk spreader both verified faithful at code level; B6-G01's RNG-stream shift is the likely mechanism for the vein divergence); re-measurement at HEAD is an open item, not a defect. (4) The 12 no-oracle drivers and 12 passing-oracle drivers were not run (execution block) — they are unmeasured, not passing.
